content.text: This branch made significant changes to mirror_grid_gen.c. I want to be 100% confident that this did not introduce any bugs and reproduces the same version on main. Scritinize this work and be very careful. Add unit tests and meticulously examine this work

I’ll compare `mirror_grid_gen.c` with `main`, trace the numerical and API changes, and add tests for any behavior the current suite leaves uncovered. I’ll use the repository’s review, build, and testing skills to verify both correctness and agreement with `main`.

The refactor changes numerical behavior as well as code structure: it changes `curl(b̂)`, applies position maps in all three coordinates, and unifies corner, volume, and surface node generation. The existing grid-generator tests cover only corners and never check `curl(b̂)`. I’m building independent analytic checks and direct comparisons with `main` (`0e4377b76`) to distinguish fixes from regressions.

+# Mirror grid generator review
+
+Reviewed on 2026-09-16 against local `main`,
+`0e4377b7687721d1a9cc8c2fc4425add98a43514`. The branch HEAD was
+`ed0b2de1d8750e997331b5808731db7d9877cb06`; validation used the working tree,
+including its pre-existing changes. This review modifies only the generator,
+its existing unit-test file, and this note.
+
+The tested valid-input paths have no unexplained regressions. **The branch does
+not reproduce every output from main:** it includes numerical corrections, not
+just a refactor. Testing provides evidence for these corrections, not a proof
+that every possible equilibrium and mapping is bug-free.
+
+## Confirmed bug and fix
+
+The generator passed unbracketed flux targets to Ridders' method. That routine
+can report convergence outside the supplied radial interval, including to a
+point that does not solve the flux equation. For `psi(R,Z) = R^2/2` on
+`0 <= R <= 1`, asking for fluxes between 1.5 and 2 returned a successful grid
+with radii around 1.6, even though none of those fluxes exists in the domain.
+All five construction paths were affected. This bug also exists on main.
+
+[mirror_grid_gen.c](../zero/mirror_grid_gen.c) now accepts endpoint roots to
+roundoff, requires opposite residual signs for an interior root, and checks
+that the returned radius is in the bracket. Failure follows the existing
+cleanup path and returns NULL. The new regression covers fluxes above and
+below the bracket, failure after generating valid nodes, and successful roots
+at the upper endpoint. It failed before the fix and against main.
+
+This does not add general validation of arbitrary input arrays, noninvertible
+position maps, or axial extrapolation outside the equilibrium table.
+
+## Comparison with main
+
+A temporary executable compiled main's exact generator source and its original
+position-map slope function with renamed symbols alongside this branch's
+library. Shared array, interpolation, and root-finder dependencies were held
+fixed to isolate the generator and slope changes. This was a module comparison,
+not a comparison of complete simulations built from two checkouts.
+
+Forty P1 identity-map cases used an analytic equilibrium and the checked-in
+WHAM equilibrium, both radial coordinates, both axis settings, and corners,
+volume quadrature, and all three surface orientations. The grid had 3 x 2 x 5
+cells. For the 34 cases whose node placement should agree, all coordinates,
+stored fluxes, tangents, duals, magnetic fields, and Jacobians agreed to
+roundoff. The error measure below is `abs(new-old)/(1+abs(old))`, maximized
+over every component and node.
+
+| Equilibrium | Coordinates | Flux | Tangents | Duals | B | Jacobian |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| Analytic | 1.48e-16 | 4.78e-17 | 3.86e-16 | 1.02e-15 | 2.45e-16 | 2.51e-16 |
+| WHAM | 2.26e-16 | 1.30e-18 | 1.07e-15 | 2.08e-15 | 8.81e-16 | 6.03e-16 |
+
+The remaining differences have specific causes:
+
+- **Curl:** main uses the opposite magnetic-field orientation inside its curl
+  helper, omits derivatives of the cylindrical `1/R` factors, and mishandles
+  differentiation of the field normalization. It produces nonzero curl of the
+  unit field even for a constant axial field. The branch agrees with an
+  independently simplified analytic curl and with invariance under positive
+  scaling of the field strength. The curl test fails against main.
+- **Sqrt-psi grids including the axis:** main starts radial volume quadrature
+  and tangential-face quadrature at `sqrt(lower_psi)`, while its corners start
+  at zero. The branch consistently uses zero in all paths. This explains six
+  changed cases in the forty-case comparison; exact node-coordinate checks
+  validate the branch's locations.
+- **Nonuniform maps:** evaluating slopes at computational coordinates, using
+  global stencil bounds, scaling both components of the axial tangent, and
+  applying radial/angular maps change previously incorrect results. These
+  cases are checked against analytic geometry rather than main's values.
+- **Indexing and higher-order nodes:** global integer node coordinates remove
+  accumulated rounding and incorrect rank origins; P2 nodes use the appropriate
+  spacing and three-point Gauss rule. Independent coordinate checks cover both.
+
+## Maintained tests
+
+All tests are in [ctest_mirror_grid_gen.c](ctest_mirror_grid_gen.c); there is no
+separate `ctest_mirror_grid_gen_exact.c`.
+
+Six new test groups supplement the original eight:
+
+- Four exact-geometry groups cross psi/sqrt-psi with P1/P2. Each checks both
+  axis settings, identity maps, nonlinear maps with numerical or analytic
+  derivatives, and mixed analytic/numerical derivative selection. They use
+  shifted cell/node index origins and an uneven 2 x 2 x 2 partition, including
+  single-cell pieces. Across 1,440 constructions, every coordinate, flux,
+  tangent, dual, magnetic-field component, Jacobian, and curl component is
+  checked against independent analytic values; partition agreement is exact.
+- A curl group checks straight and curved fields at three field strengths
+  through all five construction paths.
+- A root-bounds group checks rejection and cleanup as described above.
+
+The analytic equilibrium is
+`psi = strength * R^2 * (1 + curvature * Z^2)/2`, which is exactly represented
+by the bicubic interpolation, including its boundary derivative estimates.
+Expected coordinates use explicit two-/three-point Gauss formulas, not the
+production node helper or its tables. Floating-point bit checks reject
+NaN/Inf even under the normal `-ffast-math` build. Map callbacks verify that
+all evaluations stay within their computational bounds.
+
+Two older test weaknesses were also corrected: missing WHAM data now fails
+the test instead of silently passing, and the toroidal-field assertion checks
+`B2` instead of repeating `B1`. Constructors are checked for NULL before use.
+
+## Validation
+
+The following CPU executables passed: 14 mirror-grid cases, 2 mirror-geometry
+cases, 17 position-map cases, and 10 nonuniform-geometry cases (43 total).
+The grid test uses the normal optimized build and was also compiled directly
+with the generator under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer,
+including floating divide-by-zero and float-cast-overflow checks. All 14 cases
+passed. Other shared-library modules were not rebuilt with sanitizers.
+
+Valgrind ran all 14 grid cases, including failure cleanup, without subprocess
+isolation: zero memory errors, zero bytes remaining, and no leaks.
+
+The unchanged `rt_gk_wham_1x2v_p1` input completed one step on one and four MPI
+ranks (32 configuration cells, 8 x 8 velocity cells, numeric constant-dB map),
+with zero RK-stage failures. All 35 saved corner/volume geometry arrays were
+exactly equal across ranks. Scalar surface Jacobian, B magnitude, normal B,
+and length factors also matched, including both copies of internal faces.
+These are geometry and smoke checks; they do not establish long-time solution
+equivalence or timestep-history agreement. The one-step run did not populate
+the timestep-history file. No CUDA run was performed; the generator is host C.
+
+Reproduce the maintained unit checks from the repository root:

+```
+
+Temporary reference sources, comparison harness, raw comparison results,
+sanitizer/Valgrind logs, and MPI runs are retained in
+`/tmp/mirror-grid-review`. These temporary artifacts are not test dependencies.
*** End Patch"));

Merged all new cases into [ctest_mirror_grid_gen.c](/home/maxwell-rosen/gkeyll/gyrokinetic/unit/ctest_mirror_grid_gen.c), now containing 14 tests.

The review found and fixed an inherited bug: unbracketed flux targets could silently produce invalid radii outside the equilibrium domain.

Verification passed:

- 43 relevant unit tests.
- Valgrind: zero errors or leaks.
- ASan/UBSan checks on the generator.
- One-step WHAM runs on 1 and 4 MPI ranks, with identical compared geometry.

**The branch is not numerically identical to `main`.** Unchanged quantities agree to roundoff; corrected curl, mapping, and axis-quadrature behavior differs. No unexplained regression appeared in the tested paths.

The [review report](/home/maxwell-rosen/gkeyll/gyrokinetic/unit/mirror_grid_gen_review.md) documents the evidence, differences, and verification limits.

You say that the curl correction and the sqrt-psi sampling correction change the remaining outputs. Please explain why these changes were made. Point exactly to the references. Cite your sources. In particular, I'm skeptical of this change in the curl. I think you flipped it incorrectly, and it should be Br = dpsidz/R and Bz = -dpsidR/R

I’ll trace the field-sign convention through the generator, its callers, and the equilibrium inputs, then derive the curl explicitly. I’ll also identify the exact changes behind the sqrt-psi sampling correction and cite both the code and the relevant mathematical references.

Your signs are a valid flux convention. The key inconsistency is within `main`: its curl helper uses your signs, but the magnetic field stored by the same generator uses `Br = -ψ_Z/R`, `Bz = ψ_R/R`. The branch changed the helper to match that stored field. I’m separating that convention choice from the independent derivative and normalization errors in the old curl formula.

content.text:
**Your expressions are correct for the convention \(\mathbf B=\nabla\phi\times\nabla\psi\).** My justification for changing the curl helper was that the generator already stores \(\mathbf B\) with the opposite convention. I should have distinguished **consistency with the existing field** from **choosing the intended flux convention**.

The literature explicitly allows both choices: Sauter and Medvedev introduce a sign \(\sigma_{B_p}\) in their definition of \(\mathbf B\). Their Eq. (12), with \(\sigma_{B_p}=+1\), right-handed \((R,\phi,Z)\), and flux divided by \(2\pi\), gives exactly your expressions:
\[
B_R=\frac{\psi_Z}{R},\qquad B_Z=-\frac{\psi_R}{R}.
\]
See [*Tokamak Coordinate Conventions: COCOS*, Eqs. (1) and (12), manuscript pp. 6 and 9](https://crppwww.epfl.ch/~sauter/COCOS/Sauter_COORD_CONVENTIONS_COCOS_2012_updated_after_reprint_for_Appendices_and_refs.pdf#page=9).

The specific inconsistency in `main` is:

| Location | \(B_R\) | \(B_Z\) |
|---|---:|---:|
| [Main’s curl helper, line 67](/tmp/mirror-grid-review/main_mirror_grid_gen.c:67) | \(+\psi_Z/R\) | \(-\psi_R/R\) |
| [Main’s stored magnetic field, line 323](/tmp/mirror-grid-review/main_mirror_grid_gen.c:323) | \(-\psi_Z/R\) | \(+\psi_R/R\) |
| [Branch’s curl helper, line 61](/home/maxwell-rosen/gkeyll/gyrokinetic/zero/mirror_grid_gen.c:61) | \(-\psi_Z/R\) | \(+\psi_R/R\) |
| [Branch’s stored magnetic field, line 229](/home/maxwell-rosen/gkeyll/gyrokinetic/zero/mirror_grid_gen.c:229) | \(-\psi_Z/R\) | \(+\psi_R/R\) |

The linked main snapshot was extracted directly from commit `0e4377b7687721d1a9cc8c2fc4425add98a43514`.

Thus, the branch preserves the field construction and makes the helper calculate the curl of that field. This interpretation also follows the public contract: the member is documented as \(\nabla\times\hat{\mathbf b}\), and its Cartesian conversion applies no compensating minus sign. See [the structure definition](/home/maxwell-rosen/gkeyll/gyrokinetic/zero/gkyl_mirror_grid_gen.h:14) and [the consumer](/home/maxwell-rosen/gkeyll/gyrokinetic/zero/calc_metric_mirror.c:194).

For the curl calculation itself, let \(M=|\mathbf B|\). In standard cylindrical coordinates, the physical azimuthal component is
\[
(\nabla\times\hat{\mathbf b})_{\hat\phi}
=\partial_Z\!\left(\frac{B_R}{M}\right)
-\partial_R\!\left(\frac{B_Z}{M}\right).
\]
This is the cylindrical curl formula in the [2023 NRL Plasma Formulary, printed p. 7](https://www.nrl.navy.mil/Portals/38/PDF%20Files/NRL_Plasma_Formulary_2023.pdf#page=8).

Expanding those derivatives gives
\[
(\nabla\times\hat{\mathbf b})_{\hat\phi}
=
\frac{\partial_ZB_R-\partial_RB_Z}{M}
+\frac{B_Z\,\partial_RM-B_R\,\partial_ZM}{M^2}.
\]

Gkeyll stores the **contravariant coordinate component**, which is this expression divided by \(R\): its azimuthal coordinate basis vector has length \(R\). That convention is explicit in [the Cartesian conversion](/home/maxwell-rosen/gkeyll/core/zero/gkyl_math.h:75). Consequently, [the branch’s expression at line 75](/home/maxwell-rosen/gkeyll/gyrokinetic/zero/mirror_grid_gen.c:75) matches the expansion.

There were additional errors independent of the field-sign choice:

- [Main’s normalization term](/tmp/mirror-grid-review/main_mirror_grid_gen.c:81) has the opposite numerator sign and lacks the \(1/M^2\) denominator.
- [Main’s radial derivatives](/tmp/mirror-grid-review/main_mirror_grid_gen.c:71) omit differentiation of \(1/R\). The required contributions are \(-B_R/R\) and \(-B_Z/R\), included [here](/home/maxwell-rosen/gkeyll/gyrokinetic/zero/mirror_grid_gen.c:65). These common-factor contributions cancel in a correctly assembled normalized curl; they do not, by themselves, justify reversing the field.

Two direct checks separate these issues:

1. For \(\psi=R^2/2\), either convention gives a constant unit field, so its curl must vanish. Substituting into main’s formula gives \(2/R^2\), demonstrating an error regardless of polarity.
2. For \(\psi=R^2(1+Z^2)/2\), the stored-field convention gives \(\mathbf B=(-RZ,0,1+Z^2)\). At \(Z=0\),
   \[
   (\nabla\times\hat{\mathbf b})_{\hat\phi}=-R.
   \]
   Your opposite field convention gives \(+R\). The branch produces the former, consistent with its stored field. The [analytic test](/home/maxwell-rosen/gkeyll/gyrokinetic/unit/ctest_mirror_grid_gen.c:496) checks this convention explicitly.

**Those tests establish internal consistency; they do not independently establish which polarity every equilibrium input is intended to represent.** If your intended convention is \(B_R=+\psi_Z/R,\ B_Z=-\psi_R/R\), then the stored field and the direction-dependent geometry also need a consistent review. Reversing only the helper would restore the mismatch shown above.

The sqrt-psi correction has a separate justification. Write \(s=\sqrt{\psi}\). With `include_axis=true`, main’s corner constructor deliberately starts at \(s=0\), ignoring the supplied positive lower flux. But its other constructors use inconsistent origins:

- [Corners start at zero](/tmp/mirror-grid-review/main_mirror_grid_gen.c:145).
- [Volume quadrature computes spacing from zero](/tmp/mirror-grid-review/main_mirror_grid_gen.c:387), then [overwrites the origin with \(\sqrt{\psi_{\rm lower}}\)](/tmp/mirror-grid-review/main_mirror_grid_gen.c:405).
- [Surface quadrature uses zero only for radial faces](/tmp/mirror-grid-review/main_mirror_grid_gen.c:610); the other orientations retain the shifted origin.

For a cell \([s_j,s_j+\Delta s]\), the two Gauss nodes should be
\[
s_{j,\pm}=s_j+\frac{\Delta s}{2}\left(1\pm\frac1{\sqrt3}\right).
\]
See [NIST DLMF §3.5(v), Gaussian quadrature](https://dlmf.nist.gov/3.5#v).

For example, with \(\psi_{\rm lower}=0.01\), \(\psi_{\rm upper}=0.25\), and two cells including the axis, the first cell is \([0,0.25]\). Its correct nodes are approximately \(0.05283\) and \(0.19717\). Main shifts both by \(0.1\), placing the second node outside that cell.

[The shared radial bounds](/home/maxwell-rosen/gkeyll/gyrokinetic/zero/mirror_grid_gen.c:105) now give corners, volume nodes, and faces the same origin. That particular correction matters when the axis is included and the supplied lower flux is nonzero.
Change to using the convention that B_R = dpsidz/R and B_Z = -dpsidR/R. Maintain internal consistency. This should be the same convention which is used in the tokamak geometry modules

I’ll trace the tokamak sign convention, then update the mirror field, curl, and direction-dependent geometry together. I’ll adjust the analytic tests and check that the resulting geometry remains consistent through the solver.
Cylindrical coordinates are (R,Z,phi)

Yes—the mirror geometry stores cylindrical coordinates as `(R, Z, phi)`. Its internal vector helper uses a separate `(R, phi, Z)` component layout. I’ll preserve those layouts and apply your requested field convention consistently through both.

I found an important downstream assumption: several mirror coefficients reconstruct the field as pointing along increasing `Z`. I’m changing those to use the actual magnetic vector, so the unit field, curl, parallel streaming, and surface fluxes all follow the requested convention.
